drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's rule not to return a king's greeting apply even where refusing is dangerous, as with gentile kings?
outcomeNote: the objection to Rav Yosef is resolved by distinguishing where one can abridge; the story ends with the officer appeased

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲבָל לְמַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם — פּוֹסֵק.
segments.en: In limiting application of this principle, «Rav Yosef said: They only taught» this mishna «with regard to kings of Israel,» as a Jewish king would understand that the individual did not fail to respond to his greeting due to disrespect for the king. «However, with regard to kings of the nations of the world, he interrupts» his prayer and responds to their greeting due to the potential danger.

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל וְרָאָה אַנָּס בָּא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ, רָאָה קָרוֹן בָּא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ — לֹא יְהֵא מַפְסִיק, אֶלָּא מְקַצֵּר וְעוֹלֶה!
segments.en: The Gemara «raised an objection» to Rav Yosef’s statement: «One who is praying and saw a violent person,» feared by all, «coming toward him,» or «a carriage coming toward him» and he is in the way, «he should not stop» his prayer «but rather abridge it and move» out of the way.

segments.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאֶפְשָׁר לְקַצֵּר (יְקַצֵּר. וְאִם לָאו — פּוֹסֵק).
segments.en: The Gemara responds: This is «not difficult.» Rather, «this» that teaches to abridge one’s prayer rather than stopping, refers to a case «where it is possible to abridge» his prayer and complete it in time, in which case he «should abridge» it. «And if» it is «not» a situation where he can abridge his prayer, «he interrupts» his prayer.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָסִיד אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל בַּדֶּרֶךְ. בָּא הֶגְמוֹן אֶחָד וְנָתַן לוֹ שָׁלוֹם, וְלֹא הֶחְזִיר לוֹ שָׁלוֹם. הִמְתִּין לוֹ עַד שֶׁסִּייֵּם תְּפִלָּתוֹ. לְאַחַר שֶׁסִּייֵּם תְּפִלָּתוֹ, אָמַר לוֹ: רֵיקָא, וַהֲלֹא כָּתוּב בְּתוֹרַתְכֶם ״רַק הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ וּשְׁמֹר נַפְשְׁךָ״, וּכְתִיב ״וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם מְאֹד לְנַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם״. כְּשֶׁנָּתַתִּי לְךָ שָׁלוֹם לָמָּה לֹא הֶחְזַרְתָּ לִי שָׁלוֹם? אִם הָיִיתִי חוֹתֵךְ רֹאשְׁךָ בְּסַיִיף, מִי הָיָה תּוֹבֵעַ אֶת דָּמְךָ מִיָּדִי?!
segments.en: «The Sages taught:» There was «a» related «incident, involving a particular pious man who was praying» while traveling «along his path» when «an officer [hegmon] came and greeted him.» The pious man did not pause from his prayer «and did not respond with a greeting.» The officer «waited for him until he finished his prayer.» «After he finished his prayer,» the officer «said to him:» You «good for nothing.» You endangered yourself; I could have killed you. «Isn’t it written in your Torah: “Take utmost care and guard yourself diligently”» (Deuteronomy 4:9)? «And it is» also «written: “Take therefore good heed unto yourselves”» (Deuteronomy 4:15)? Why did you ignore the danger to your life? «When I greeted you, why did you not respond with a greeting?» «Were I to sever your head with a sword, who would hold me accountable for your» spilled «blood?»

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ: הַמְתֵּן לִי עַד שֶׁאֲפַיֶּיסְךָ בִּדְבָרִים. אָמַר לוֹ: אִילּוּ הָיִיתָ עוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם, וּבָא חֲבֵרְךָ וְנָתַן לְךָ שָׁלוֹם — הָיִיתָ
segments.en: The pious man «said to him: Wait for me until I will appease you with» my «words.» «He said to him: Had you been standing before a flesh and blood king and your friend came and greeted you,» would «you» «return his» greeting?

segments.he: מַחֲזִיר לוֹ?! אָמַר לוֹ: לָאו. וְאִם הָיִיתָ מַחֲזִיר לוֹ, מָה הָיוּ עוֹשִׂים לְךָ? אָמַר לוֹ: הָיוּ חוֹתְכִים אֶת רֹאשִׁי בְּסַיִיף. אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר, וּמָה אַתָּה שֶׁהָיִיתָ עוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם, שֶׁהַיּוֹם כָּאן וּמָחָר בַּקֶּבֶר — כָּךְ אֲנִי שֶׁהָיִיתִי עוֹמֵד לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁהוּא חַי וְקַיָּים לָעַד וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים — עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
segments.en: The officer «said to him: No.» The pious man continued: «And if you would» greet «him, what would they do to you?» The officer «said to him: They would cut» off «my head with a sword.» The pious man «said to him: Isn’t this matter an a fortiori inference?» «You who were standing before a king of flesh and blood,» of whom your fear is limited «because today he is here but tomorrow he is in the grave,» would have reacted in «that» way; «I, who was standing» and praying «before the Supreme King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He,» «Who lives and endures for all eternity,» «all the more so» that I could not pause to respond to someone’s greeting.

segments.he: מִיָּד נִתְפַּיֵּיס אוֹתוֹ הֶגְמוֹן, וְנִפְטַר אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד לְבֵיתוֹ לְשָׁלוֹם.
segments.en: When he heard this, «the officer was immediately appeased and the pious man returned home in peace.»

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף, לא שנו אלא למלכי ישראל
moves.summary: Rav Yosef limits the mishna to Jewish kings; for gentile kings one interrupts
moves.about: the mishna's rule not to return a king's greeting applies only to kings of Israel; for gentile kings one interrupts because of danger

moves.summary: objects from a baraita: one seeing a violent man does not stop but abridges
moves.about: the baraita says not to stop even for a dangerous person, against Rav Yosef's ruling that one interrupts for gentile kings

moves.summary: resolves: abridge where possible, interrupt where not
moves.about: reconciles the baraita with Rav Yosef: where one can abridge and finish he abridges; where he cannot, he interrupts

moves.summary: cites the baraita: a pious man praying did not return an officer's greeting
moves.about: the baraita recounting the pious man who did not return an officer's greeting while praying

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: ריקא, והלא כתוב בתורתכם
moves.summary: the officer challenges: the Torah commands guarding life, why did you not respond
moves.about: why the pious man endangered his life by not returning the greeting, when the Torah commands guarding one's life

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: אילו היית עומד לפני מלך בשר ודם
moves.summary: the pious man asks whether he would return a greeting before a mortal king
moves.about: whether, standing before a mortal king, the officer would return a friend's greeting
the officer answers that he would not return the greeting before a mortal king

moves.cueHe: ואם היית מחזיר לו, מה היו עושים לך
moves.summary: asks what would be done to him had he returned it
moves.about: what would be done to the officer had he returned a greeting before a mortal king

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: היו חותכים את ראשי בסייף
moves.summary: the officer answers: they would behead me
moves.about: the officer answers that they would behead him

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: והלא דברים קל וחומר
moves.summary: a fortiori: all the more so before the eternal King of kings
moves.about: a fortiori: if one does not return a greeting before a mortal king, all the more so before the eternal King of kings

moves.summary: the officer is appeased and the pious man goes home in peace
moves.about: the officer accepts the pious man's a fortiori argument and is appeased
